Tuesday 27 October 2026 · 25 stories
Morning Brief
Nifty 50 rose 0.68% to 22,753 on narrow participation
Today’s read
The biggest names carried the session. The fifty most traded stocks returned +3.21% weighted by turnover, against +0.32% for the median stock, a gap of 2.9 percentage points, so most stocks did worse than the busiest names suggest.

Mahindra Logistics Limited rose 5.4% on 62 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about guidance or investor update, “Outcome of meeting with Analysts/ Institutional Investors/ Funds. Detailed disclosure is attached.”.

Steel Strips Wheels Limited rose 13.6% on 48 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about guidance or investor update, “Investor Presentation”.

Tata Teleservices (Maharashtra) Limited rose 10.2% on 104 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Stocks in news: Paytm, Tata Consumer, Dalmia Bharat, REC and DCM Shriram”.

Nothing in the news or in exchange filings explains the volume in DCM Shriram Industries Limited (64x), Permanent Magnets Limited (49x), Jindal Poly Films Limited (42x). That usually points to a sector story rather than a company one.

What happened
Breaking
Stock markets rebound after 4-day slump; Sensex jumps 483 points
The Nifty 50 ended a four-session decline to gain 153 points, driven by short covering across metal and healthcare stocks. While this provides temporary relief, sustained foreign portfolio investor outflows continue to cap broad market earnings multiples, particularly in financial and automotive sectors. Net institutional flow data in coming sessions will confirm if foreign selling is abating or merely pausing.

Tata Motors completes Iveco acquisition to turbocharge global play
Tata Motors completed its 4.5 billion dollar acquisition of Italian commercial vehicle maker Iveco to expand across European and Latin American markets. The deal strengthens Tata Motors' heavy commercial vehicle portfolio, though increased debt and integration expenses will likely compress consolidated operating margins over the next few quarters. Deleveraging timelines in the upcoming quarterly filing will indicate the balance sheet stretch.

Paytm achieved operating profitability in its September quarter earnings, while Dalmia Bharat reported cement margins constrained by weak regional pricing. Paytm's reduced cash burn stabilizes valuation multiples for listed fintechs, whereas Dalmia's performance reflects persistent cement price pressure across eastern India despite declining petcoke costs. Price realization metrics in upcoming cement channel checks will clarify near-term profitability trends for regional producers.

Top IT stocks to buy after Q2 results: TCS vs Infosys vs Wipro vs HCL vs Tech Mahindra - What market experts recommend
Brokerage recommendations following second-quarter IT results favor HCLTech and TCS over Tech Mahindra due to steady deal execution. Tier-one Indian IT companies face divergent earnings trajectories as weak discretionary technology spending in North America weighs on revenue growth. Deal total contract value disclosures over coming quarters will show whether revenue conversion accelerates across these vendors.

Steel Strips Wheels zooms 36% in two days; what's driving auto parts stock?
Steel Strips Wheels surged 36 percent in two sessions, with 15.5 percent of total equity changing hands on unusually high trading volume. Large secondary market transactions often signal institutional accumulation or promoter reallocations, influencing free float and trading liquidity across small-cap auto ancillary stocks. Exchange filings on bulk and block deals will confirm whether strategic or financial investors acquired these stakes.

Tata Communications targets 40% of India's data centre connectivity market with ₹4,350 crore investment
Tata Communications is deploying ₹4,350 crore to lay a 10,000-kilometre fibre network along the Mumbai-Pune-Hyderabad-Chennai corridor. This capital expenditure increases near-term balance sheet leverage and depresses return on capital employed for the company. However, securing long-term enterprise bandwidth contracts from hyperscalers could expand consolidated EBITDA margins as capacity utilization rises.

Delayed equipment deliveries will extend dependence on imported cells, pressuring near-term gross margins and slowing earnings growth for domestic manufacturers.

This order backlog offers over four times trailing revenue visibility, strengthening earnings predictability for the defence electronics supplier. ISMA says 107 sugar mills begin crushing operations so far, enough stock to meet domestic demand
The sugar industry body reported 107 mills starting crushing operations, confirming adequate inventory for domestic demand. Sufficient carry-forward stock limits immediate upside in ex-mill sugar prices, capping near-term gross margin expansion for listed millers like Balrampur Chini Mills and Triveni Engineering. Sector earnings now depend on government ethanol allocation quotas and divertible sucrose pricing decisions.

Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Tuesday
The Nifty 50 recovered 153 points to close at 24,339 on Monday, snapping a four-day losing streak. The rebound provides transient relief, but sustained foreign institutional selling exceeding ₹1 trillion this month continues to pressure broad valuations across large-cap financials and IT. Daily FPI net turnover data over the next two sessions will clarify if institutional support is genuinely returning.

Anthropic opens books on AI's explosive growth and staggering costs
Anthropic disclosed mounting compute costs alongside rapid revenue growth in its preliminary listing documents. Escalating model training expenditures underscore that generative AI deployment remains capital intensive. For Indian IT services majors like Infosys and TCS, high infrastructure costs threaten operational margins as clients demand broader AI integration. Upcoming quarterly capital expenditure updates from US hyperscalers will confirm global tech spending trajectory.

NBFCs curb fresh loans in rural markets as weak monsoon raises repayment risks
Shriram Finance and Bajaj Finance are reducing fresh loan disbursements in drought-hit rural districts to contain repayment risks. Slower disbursement velocity will weigh on net interest margins and assets under management growth for retail non-banking financial companies. The upcoming quarterly asset quality disclosures, specifically early-stage delinquencies in rural vehicle and micro-loans, will show the full impact on credit costs.

Can SFC Environmental Technologies IPO deliver long-term growth for high-risk investors?
SFC Environmental Technologies filed draft prospectus papers to raise ₹150 crore in fresh equity alongside a ₹517.5 crore secondary offer. Debt repayment using fresh proceeds will lower annual interest expense, lifting net profit margins in municipal water treatment projects. The final prospectus disclosures on working capital cycles and customer concentration will confirm whether operating cash flows can support execution.

Rising concentration in AI stocks poses a risk: Kunal Kapoor, Morningstar CEO
Morningstar Chief Executive Kunal Kapoor warned that extreme portfolio concentration in high-valuation AI stocks creates systemic equity market risk. A valuation derating in global tech heavyweights could trigger broad risk-off sentiment, accelerating foreign institutional portfolio outflows from Indian equities. Institutional fund flow tracking in emerging market equity funds over coming weeks will confirm if global asset allocation is shifting toward defensive assets.

Three challenges facing HDFC Bank’s new CEO
HDFC Bank faces executive attrition alongside pressure to improve its credit-deposit ratio following its merger with HDFC Ltd. Management stability and deposit growth rates govern valuation multiples across the private banking sector, directly affecting benchmark index weights. Deposit growth figures in upcoming quarterly filings will confirm whether funding costs stabilize.

Google CEO Sundar Pichai says company is giving up short-term cloud revenue to prioritise advanced AI development
Alphabet is reallocating cloud compute capacity to internal artificial intelligence research, limiting server allocation for corporate clients through 2027. This compute bottleneck threatens to delay enterprise cloud migration and AI implementation projects executed by Indian IT exporters like Infosys and TCS. Deal TCVs in upcoming quarterly updates will show whether cloud capacity constraints slow client project deployments.

Tata Consumer Q2 Results: Net profit rises 16% YoY to Rs 470 crore, revenue up 14%
Tata Consumer Products reported an 18% increase in Q2 EBITDA to Rs 794 crore, with revenues expanding 14% to Rs 5,661 crore on strong tea and salt volumes. Margin expansion in core branded business buffers input cost volatility, protecting profitability across FMCG majors. India retail volume growth in Q3 will confirm whether consumer demand survives ongoing food inflation.

Sunteck Realty H1FY27 net profit rises 20%, pre-sales up 19%
Sunteck Realty posted H1 FY27 pre-sales of Rs 1,611 crore, up 19% year-on-year, while net profit rose 20% to Rs 99 crore. Consistent pre-sales growth improves cash flow visibility, supporting balance sheet deleveraging for mid-cap premium real estate developers. Operating cash flow numbers in the next filing will show if pre-sales translate into timely project collections.
ET Markets
Dalmia Bharat posts Rs 205 crore Q2 loss on exceptional hit
Dalmia Bharat posted a Q2 consolidated net loss of Rs 205 crore due to a Rs 339 crore exceptional charge for asset impairment and staff rationalization, despite volume rising 3%. Operational earnings demonstrate ongoing cement sector margin compression driven by subdued regional realization rates. Realization per ton in Q3 results will confirm whether pricing discipline returns to eastern regional markets.

India’s outward FDI falls 14% to $4.34 billion in September as loans, guarantees decline
India’s outward foreign direct investment dropped 37% month-on-month to $4.34 billion in September, led by a 20% reduction in foreign equity commitments. Slower outbound capital deployment reduces capital export pressures, helping preserve foreign exchange reserves and domestic banking system liquidity. October outbound FDI data from the Reserve Bank of India will show whether overseas corporate expansion plans are slowing permanently.

India and US fine-tune trade pact after concluding most talks, says Piyush Goyal
India and the United States completed primary bilateral trade negotiations, entering the final text fine-tuning stage. Reciprocal tariff reductions will lower trade friction, expanding operating margins and order volumes for export-dependent sectors like generic pharmaceuticals, textiles, and engineering goods. The forthcoming joint tariff schedule will confirm the precise margin impact and duty cuts across listed industries.

FTA with India will be a game changer in supply chain management: EU ambassador to India
European Union Ambassador Jean-Eric Paquet stated that ongoing India-EU Free Trade Agreement talks aim to integrate bilateral supply chains under a unified framework. Tariff elimination will lower input costs for imported European capital goods, benefiting domestic industrial machinery and auto component manufacturers. Lower non-tariff barriers will simultaneously improve gross margins and market access for specialty chemicals and textiles.
